_readme: Per-STEP figures for the few entries that are a sequence of different movements
rather than one movement. Keyed by exercise slug, then by index into that entry's
NOTHING HERE IS NEW ARTWORK. Each step borrows a pose from a figure that already
exists and has already been reviewed, and adds its own arrows. `use` is the figure
slug; `frame` picks one pose from it (omit to play that figure's own movement);
`arrows` replaces the borrowed figure's arrows with the ones this step needs.
WHY ARROWS DO THE WORK. Five of the warm-up's eight steps are CIRCLES - wrist,
shoulder, ankle, hip, and the trunk turn. A circle is a path, not a pose, so no
pair of stills can show one, and the image model cannot draw one either. An arrow
is a path. Hence loop arrows (cx, cy, r) alongside the original arc form.
Coordinates are in the borrowed figure's own space, which is why they differ so
much between entries - read them off the figure, do not guess.

joint-mobilising-sequence.step: Stand on one leg, circle the raised ankle
Hands on hips, circle the hips
Turn the upper body to each side
Finish with a minute of marching
